yes_case.case: The closest past episodes are the rollout of the FME Phase-II scheme for electric vehicles in 2019 and the PM E-Drive Scheme approved in late 2024. This current e-bus and e-truck financing scheme differs from the 2019 FME Phase-II because that framework focused primarily on broad demand aggregation and upfront consumer purchase subsidies rather than targeted interest subsidies and credit guarantees for heavy commercial vehicle manufacturers and operators. It differs from the 2024 PM E-Drive Scheme because that initiative was an umbrella allocation with caps and generalized EV support, whereas the upcoming heavy industries financing scheme is specifically calibrated to de-risk commercial debt and provide targeted credit guarantees tailored exclusively to the high capital expenditure required for electric buses and trucks. The structural push to de-risk heavy commercial EV financing mirrors the mechanism used successfully in prior industrial sector credit-linked capital goods schemes, making the formal gazette notification highly aligned with established Ministry playbook precedents.

no_case.case: The closest past episodes are the rollout of the FAME II scheme adjustments in 2021 and the formulation of the PM-EBus Sewa scheme in late 2023. Unlike the FAME iterations which leveraged existing bureaucratic channels for vehicle purchase incentives, a dedicated financing scheme for commercial e-trucks and e-buses requires novel risk-sharing architectures between public financial institutions and private lenders, making it structurally distinct and vastly more prone to bureaucratic friction than past precedent suggests.
